company_name: Qfin Holdings, Inc. (formerly Qifu Technology / 360 DigiTech)
model: Lender FCFE at cost of equity (net income less capital retained for loan-book growth, excess capital in bridge; engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Excess capital above risk-bearing requirement, after PRC withholding and stress haircut
equity_bridge.note: 30-Jun-2026 attributable equity RMB24,750m less H1-2026 dividend declared (US$0.46 x 121.58m ADS x 6.7851 = RMB379m) = RMB24,371m. Required/non-distributable: 22% x RMB53,579m risk-bearing balance (107,562 total - 53,983 capital-light/ICE/tech; Q2-2026 release) = RMB11,787m, + PP&E 641 + land use rights 956 + DTA 1,567 = RMB14,951m. Gross excess RMB9,420m x 0.9 (10% PRC dividend withholding on repatriation) x 0.6 (40% haircut: the late-June-2026 industry liquidity shock, possible regulatory/funding-partner demands for thicker capital, and cash trapped in PRC entities) = RMB5,087m. Its earnings are stripped from the margin path.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026E-FY2036 revenue CAGR (~3%). Historical CAGRs (FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025) are pre-reset: FY2026E revenue is ~-29% and net income ~-60% after the Oct-2025 24% APR cap, the 2026 industry contraction and the June-2026 funding shock, so none of them is a forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 8.5% vs EPS 3yr 20.4% and equity 5yr 20.6% vs revenue 5yr 7.2% -- >30% divergence. Equity growth was suppressed by RMB8.4bn of buybacks/dividends FY2024-25; EPS was flattered by a 15% share-count reduction. FCF CAGRs are on OCF - capex - SBC, which for a lender omits loan-book investment and is not meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income immaterial) grows at the same rate as reported FCF: SBC is ~2% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow. Both series overstate distributable cash because loan originations sit in investing activities.

scenario_narratives.base: The industry shakeout runs through 2027: loan balance keeps shrinking (-23% YoY at Jun-2026) and FY2027 revenue falls another 5% from the FY2026E RMB13.6bn run-rate, then the platform grows mid-single digits as weaker facilitators exit and QFIN's repeat-borrower franchise (89% of volume) and 168 funding partners take share. Margins rebuild from the Q3-2026 trough as provisions normalise and S&M stays disciplined, but stop well short of the pre-cap 37%: the 24% all-in APR cap is permanent, take rates in capital-light/ICE are structurally lower and the tax holiday is gone. ROE on required capital settles ~18%, about 2.5x what the market price implies on book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The June-2026 liquidity shock proves to be the clearing event. Funding conditions normalise in 2027, the new risk-officer CEO (Yan Zheng, from 21-Sep-2026) tightens underwriting without losing volume, competitors exit, and overseas (Indonesia/Mexico-style) lending under Haisheng Wu adds a second leg. Revenue regains FY2025 levels by ~2029 and pre-tax margins reach 30% -- still below FY2024-25 because pricing is capped.
scenario_narratives.bear: The liquidity shock becomes a credit event. Bank and trust partners cut funding, the 2025-26 vintages sour (90-day+ delinquency was already 3.5% at Mar-2026), and a further regulatory squeeze -- a lower APR cap, curbs on credit-assistance/guarantee arrangements, or caps on platform market share -- forces a disorderly shrink: revenue -25% and -15% in 2027-28, a pre-tax loss of ~25% of revenue in 2027 (~RMB2.6bn, ~7% of on-balance loans) and breakeven in 2028. The business survives as a smaller, 12%-margin facilitator growing with nominal consumer credit; half the capital released by runoff is held back by regulators. Not modelled: a 2020-P2P-style outright prohibition or VIE expropriation, which the 3pp ADR premium in the discount rate, not the flows, is charging.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a credit platform with RMB36bn of loans on its own balance sheet as a lender: equity holders own net income after funding costs and provisions, less the capital the book needs to grow, discounted at an RMB cost of equity with a China-ADR structural premium. The price (~0.22x June-2026 book, ~2.5x FY2026E underlying earnings) implies the market expects most of the book to be lost, trapped or expropriated; the model's bear case -- a ~RMB2.6bn loss year, revenue down 36% over two years and half the released capital withheld -- still values the ADS above the quote. The gap is therefore a bet on PRC policy and ADS-holder access to capital, not on the operating model, and is sized accordingly in the weights and the 14% CoE.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory: further APR cap reductions, restrictions on credit-assistance/guarantee (capital-heavy) arrangements, or platform market-share limits from PBOC/NFRA.
Funding: the late-June-2026 industry-wide liquidity shock; bank and trust partners can withdraw quickly, forcing a smaller book.
Credit: 90-day+ delinquency 3.50% at Mar-2026 and 2.83% at Jun-2026; Day-1 delinquency 5.6% -- a consumer-credit downturn hits on-balance loans directly.
Structure: Cayman issuer controlling PRC licences via VIE contracts; HFCAA/delisting risk on the ADS; repatriation of excess capital subject to PRC approval and 10% withholding.
Excess-capital estimate: the 22% risk-capital ratio and 40% haircut are judgments; every RMB1bn in the bridge is ~US$1.2/ADS.
Governance: CEO change on 20-Sep-2026 (founder-era CEO moved to international); management guidance only one quarter ahead.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.245-30.58; parity-checked against 3660.HK.
data_sources.financials: QFIN_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2016-FY2025; figures are RMB despite the USD label) and the 6-K earnings releases for Q4-2025, Q1-2026 and Q2-2026 (Extracted/QFIN_Quarterly_*.txt), including the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet and Q3-2026 guidance.
data_sources.qualitative: Q2-2026 release management commentary (industry contraction, June liquidity shock, prudent growth), 20-Sep-2026 management-change 6-K. No Analysis.json existed at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: Millions of ADS (1 ADS = 2 Class A ordinary shares), so every per-share value is per ADS and comparable to the Nasdaq quote. 123.61m = Q2-2026 weighted diluted ADS (247.22m diluted ordinary shares / 2; Q2-2026 release). Ordinary shares outstanding 30-Jun-2026 were 243,165,684 (121.58m ADS); the gap is unvested RSUs/options. The remaining ~US$113m of 2030 convertible notes is deep out of the money at this price and is already deducted inside book equity, so it is not added to the count. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Q4/FY release non-GAAP reconciliation (RMB378.4m, QFIN_Quarterly_Q4-2025.txt:719); H1-2026 RMB119.6m (QFIN_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:619). No separate net-share-settlement tax line disclosed in the releases.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in RMB (ISO CNY); quote is USD per ADS. fx_rate 0.149282 USD per CNY = 1/6.6987 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-10-03 21:32Z). Parity check against the HKEX line 3660.HK: HK$25.80 x 2 shares/ADS / 7.8463 HKD per USD = US$6.58 vs the Nasdaq ADS print, a ~1.8% gap explained by the HK close preceding the NY close by ~12 hours on a falling tape. The Metrics.csv Currency column says USD -- that is the XBRL mislabel seen on BILI/FUTU; the figures are RMB (FY2025 revenue RMB19,205m ties to the Q4-2025 release).
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (H1-2026 actual RMB7,476m revenue + H2 at Q3-2026 guidance run-rate ~RMB3.06bn/quarter)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is post-funding-cost FCFE, so it is discounted at CoE and no debt is deducted afterwards. Built in RMB: China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta 1.4 (levered consumer lender, single-regulator) x 6.5% China ERP = 11.0%, plus a 3.0pp China-ADR structural premium = 14.0%. The premium charges risks the scenarios do NOT model: VIE structure (the operating licences sit in PRC consolidated entities the Cayman issuer controls only by contract), HFCAA/delisting exposure of the ADS (mitigated, not removed, by the HKEX 3660 secondary listing), and capital-repatriation friction from PRC subsidiaries. Operating/regulatory earnings risk (APR caps, funding-partner withdrawal, credit losses) is charged in the scenario flows and weights only -- the same 14% applies to every scenario, so risk is not charged twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial; leases are office space inside operating expenses. No lease line in the flows, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is RMB34m of equity and runs at a small loss (RMB8m H1-2026); flows are taken at consolidated level and the NCI is ignored as immaterial (<0.2% of book).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: QFIN is routed to the lender row of dcf-methods/SKILL.md, not owner-FCF. Although marketed as capital-light credit-tech, at 30-Jun-2026 it carried RMB36.2bn of on-balance-sheet loans receivable (Fuzhou Microcredit + consolidated trusts) funded by RMB18.1bn payable to trust investors and RMB2.2bn short-term loans, plus guarantee liabilities on off-balance capital-heavy loans; 50% of the RMB107.6bn platform balance (RMB53.6bn) carries QFIN principal risk. Loan originations run through INVESTING cash flow, so OCF - capex (FY2025 RMB10.8bn, 1.8x net income) is not owner cash; provisions are added back in OCF while the losses they fund leave via investing. Trust payables are operating funding, not net debt (the 'deposits are not net debt' rule). The flow is therefore bank-style FCFE: revenue x pre-tax-pre-SBC margin (ebitda_margin_path; D&A and capex both set to 0 because pre-tax income is already after D&A of ~RMB70m/yr and capex is HQ/land of similar size) - SBC - cash tax, LESS capital retained to grow the risk-bearing book (wc_capture_pct = -90: each RMB1 of revenue growth needs ~RMB0.9 of equity; a shrinking book releases it). Excess capital above that requirement is added once in equity_bridge, and its earnings (avoided funding cost ~3% pre-tax on ~RMB9bn, ~2pp of margin; net interest income RMB62m in H1-2026) are stripped from the margin path so it is not counted twice. Valuation clock: FY0 is FY2026E and Y1 is FY2027; the 30-Jun-2026 book already holds H1 earnings, and H2-2026 earnings (~RMB0.8bn) less the RMB0.38bn H1 dividend are left out as an offset to discounting Y1 a full year from October. Buybacks: RMB4.85bn FY2025 and RMB2.97bn FY2024 (US$450m 2025 plan fully used; March-2025 plan US$234m used), but share count has been flat at ~243m ordinary through 2026 -- buybacks have effectively stopped and cash went to repurchasing the 2030 converts (US$577m principal retired for US$502m by May-2026). Dividend policy ~30% of GAAP NI: US$0.78/ADS for H2-2025, US$0.46/ADS for H1-2026 (paid ~1-Oct-2026). Analysis.json did not exist at build time; qualitative inputs are from the Q4-2025, Q1-2026 and Q2-2026 releases and the 20-Sep-2026 CEO change 6-K (Extracted/).

bear.wc_capture_pct_note: Only half of the capital a shrinking book releases reaches shareholders; the rest is absorbed by tighter capital demands from regulators and funding partners.

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-tax, pre-SBC margin net of the ~2pp funding benefit of excess capital. Y1 17% ~ Q3-2026 guided run-rate (non-GAAP NI RMB400-500m/qtr => ~19% pre-tax) less the strip; recovers to 26% by Y5 vs 31% FY2023 and 37% FY2025 (pre-cap) because the 24% all-in APR cap is permanent.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: 25% PRC statutory (the Q2-2026 RMB500m one-off reflects the authorities withdrawing preferential treatment for certain entities) + ~1pp for withholding on the distributed share.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Capital retained for book growth: ~0.87x revenue of risk capital (RMB11.8bn / RMB13.6bn) rounded to 0.9.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 9x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 35% from the 15% house default: single-regulator dependency in a sector the PBOC/NFRA has repeatedly reset, a live industry funding shock, Q3-2026 net-income guidance -67% to -73% YoY, and an unexplained CEO change one month after results. Base 45% because the balance sheet (RMB24.8bn equity vs RMB53.6bn risk-bearing balance) can absorb a severe loss year without a raise. Bull cut to 20% because it needs funding normalisation, benign credit and no further rule change simultaneously.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
sanity_check.known_limitation: core_metrics.currency is mislabeled USD for every QFIN row (actual reporting currency is CNY) due to a documented bug in build_facts_xbrl.py that hardcodes currency="USD" for all SEC XBRL extractions regardless of the XBRL unit tag (see memory: build-facts-xbrl-hardcodes-usd-currency.md, also seen on BILI, HDB, MFG). Because quote_currency is also USD (correct, Nasdaq ADR), sanity_check.py historical_table() never triggers its row_currency != quote_currency FX-conversion guard, so historical P/E, P/B and P/Sales divide RMB-mislabeled-as-USD financials by the real USD price -- both sides wrong by the ~6.7x CNY/USD rate, canceling to a coincidentally plausible-looking but meaningless multiple (reported pe=1.35, pb=0.31). This is the same false-pass mechanism documented for HDB/MFG/HSBC. The dcf-analyst correctly set inputs.currency=CNY/fx_rate for the actual valuation build, so the DCF itself (intrinsic value, scenario multiples quoted in the agent report) is NOT affected -- only this sanity_check block's historical_table/implied_multiples are unreliable until build_facts_xbrl.py is fixed to thread the real XBRL unit through instead of hardcoding USD.
